about: Every node of the design loop and verification chain: what it reads, what it writes, the parameters it runs with and the rules it applies. tools/pipeline.py reads its parameters from here (a changed parameter is a changed node); docs/NODES.md and the V&V report are generated from this file (python3 tools/nodes_doc.py).

nodes.does: The customer case: orbit, mass properties, surfaces, requirements and budgets (adcs-case/1).
rules: every requirement names its source (stated by the user, or UNCONFIRMED with a plan reference)
the case file is part of every cached run's key: a changed requirement re-flies the matrix

nodes.does: Bought actuators as their datasheets state them: CubeSpace, AAC Clyde Space and Rocket Lab reaction wheels, Tensor Tech control moment gyroscopes. One file per model with the datasheet numbers, the source URL and the model parameters derived from them (each derived value says how).
inputs: vendor datasheets and product pages (source_url in every file)
rules: a number not on the datasheet is null in the datasheet block, never guessed
model parameters the engine needs but the datasheet omits (rotor inertia, friction, imbalance) are derived and marked derived, with the rule
RW, CMG and VSCMG are bought: they are selected from the catalogue, never sized by a law

nodes.does: What the case asks of an actuator: one orbit on the POP orbit at four held attitudes with the SILS torque models; peak disturbance, cyclic and secular momentum, weakest field, detumble and slew momentum.
rules: h_req = k_h x max(cyclic + secular per orbit, slew momentum)
tau_req = k_tau x max(peak disturbance, slew torque)
fine class when req.ake <= 0.05 deg (star tracker, precision gyro)

nodes.does: Our magnetorquer coils, sized: the largest of the dumping, momentum and detumble dipoles.

parameters.anchor: SYN-CT-1: mass 0.03 kg, 0.3 W per 0.45 Am2

rules: m = max(2 tau_dist/(0.5 B_min), 2 h_secular/(0.3 B_mean T), h_detumble/(0.3 B_mean t_detumble/2))
the coils-only family carries the pointing-grade coil (at least twice the dumping dipole)

nodes.does: Our fluid momentum loop, one ring per axis, designed with its electromagnetic DC conduction pump (no permanent magnet).
rules: grid over flow speed, bore, gap field and pump length; keep the least mass + lambda x steady power that meets h_req and tau_req
torque capacity = I_max B / b x 2 S A / L; coil m_cu = sqrt(lambda K)

nodes.does: Our N2O cold-gas RCS, 6 couples: thrust class and propellant tank.
rules: thrust: the smallest class above the couple the detumble and slew need
propellant: detumble + dumping over life, 1.2 margin

nodes.does: The benchmarks' momentum actuators chosen from the catalogue: for RW three orthogonal wheels, for CMG and VSCMG a four-unit 54.74 deg pyramid.
outputs: parts/<catalogue part>.json (the chosen model, with the modelling block the engine flies)

per_unit_need.rw: h >= h_req x scale, tau >= tau_req x scale
per_unit_need.cmg: rotor h >= h_req/2 x scale, gimbal torque h x gimbal rate >= tau_req x scale
per_unit_need.vscmg: as cmg; a CMG whose datasheet allows a variable rotor speed, else the CMG operated at variable speed (marked assumption)

parameters.choose: the lightest model that meets the need; ties by steady power, then volume

rules: when no model meets the need the largest is taken and the gap is reported (the loop cannot size it up)
an authority increase from the converge node raises the need, so the next model up is chosen

nodes.does: The sensor set of every product: magnetometer, six sun sensors, gyro, GNSS, Earth sensor; the star tracker on the fine class or when knowledge asks for it.
rules: gyro grade g: noise x g, mass and power / g (fibre-optic class below 1)

nodes.does: Each family's product: mass, steady power and volume summed over every fitted unit.
rules: units per fill = number of axes / spin axes / boresights; the six sun sensors count as one part

nodes.runs_in: Rust engine + C flight software (adcs run)
nodes.does: Every mission mode x actuator option x seed on the sized products; options that fail on performance also fly every algorithm of their slot.

parameters.cache_key: scenario, product, parts, seed, flight-software build, case file

rules: a run is scored against the case's requirements at run time
channels are deleted after scoring (the manifest is kept)

nodes.does: Per option: feasible on every seed? Each failing requirement classed; the best algorithm per option kept.
rules: rank an option's variants by (not feasible, failing count, worst objective)

nodes.does: The knob changes the failures call for; converged when nothing is left to change.
rules: performance: fly every algorithm of the slot, then (fluid loop) a quieter flow sensor /4, then authority x1.5; undone when the violation does not fall by 5 %
rate stability (fine class): gyro noise x0.3 down to x0.1; undone when it does not improve
knowledge: fit the star tracker on a coarse product
power, fluid loop: pump lambda x3 (not for RCS valve power); coils-only: coil authority x0.75; rotors: blocked (standby power is the floor)

mass over budget, closest solution family: lighter gyro, one star-tracker head, lambda /3, fluid-loop momentum x0.75 -- each undone and closed if it breaks a mode or raises the violation by more than 5 %
propellant: RCS x1.5
a part pushed up by one failure and down by another is frozen and reported as a conflict

nodes.does: Scores every family (ours and the benchmarks) on the same modes and budget, then picks the minimum feasible solution; the benchmarks are ranked by the same rule as the comparison.

parameters.feasible: every mode passes with a usable option on every seed, and mass <= req.mass, volume <= req.vol

rules: selected = the feasible solution family first in rank_feasible order (least mass, then power, then volume)
when no solution family is feasible the closest one is named with its gaps
benchmark = the same ranking over the benchmark families, reported beside the selection

nodes.does: The selected family's mission (detumble -> Sun acquisition -> nadir), its adcs-fswcfg/1 blob, the converged products; C and Rust checked bit-identical.
rules: the C and Rust flight software must agree bit for bit

nodes.does: Monte Carlo of the dispatched mission with the case's dispersions (truth dispersed, flight software nominal).
rules: dispersions as asils.campaign.draw

nodes.does: The dispatched mission with the flight software as firmware (C and Rust) beside its SILS run; exact instruction timing and bus latency.
rules: a latency >= the control step counts as an overrun
a missing instruction count stops the run

nodes.does: The design ledger per case and the V&V report (HTML and PDF).
rules: every table is generated from the stored node outputs, never typed
